Choose an SSD that fits the socket and workload

M.2 describes a shape, not a complete interface

Check the computer or console documentation for supported interface, physical length and clearance. A 2.5-inch SATA drive and an M.2 NVMe drive are not direct substitutes. An enclosure can be sold alongside search results for complete drives; verify that storage is actually included. For a laptop upgrade, check whether mounting hardware and any required thermal parts are already present.

Capacity and advertised speed need a use case

Allow for the operating system, games or project files and keep a backup before replacing a drive. Compare sustained-write information and warranty terms if you regularly move large files. A peak sequential-read claim is not a prediction of every application's loading speed. For used drives, ask for health and usage information; a low price alone does not establish remaining endurance.

How we choose these daily picks

Our product comparisons are built using current retailer data, market analysis and available marketplace feedback to identify the products most worthy of consideration. We do not rely on promotional messaging, manufacturer claims or advertised discounts when making recommendations. Instead, we focus on products that demonstrate strong value, positive seller signals and a credible marketplace track record. Although we have not physically tested every item featured, our methodology is designed to help consumers make informed and confident purchasing decisions. Where performance, safety or durability are especially important, we also encourage checking independent reviews of the exact model.
